question: Which of the following is classified as a DISTAL (upstream) determinant of community health status?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Poverty is a distal social determinant that shapes living conditions, nutrition, education, and access to care — all upstream influences on health.
Incorrect. This is a proximate (immediate) biological determinant — the direct infectious agent causing disease, not an upstream social driver.
Incorrect. Low immunisation coverage is an intermediate determinant (a health-system behaviour), not a distal social determinant like poverty or education.

answers.text: High diarrhoeal disease incidence in children under five

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. This is a health outcome measure, not a determinant. Determinants are factors that influence health status, not the disease itself.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the determinants framework: distal (poverty, education, governance) → intermediate (living conditions, health behaviours) → proximate (biological exposures). Try again.
Well done. Distal determinants like poverty operate far upstream, shaping the conditions in which communities live, work, and access healthcare.
